title: There's a stress gap between men and women ｜ 男女之间存在着压力差距

sents.en: "I used to work very hard.
sents.cn: "我以前工作非常拼命。

sents.en: I love to create things, grow them and solve problems," said Meng Li, a successful app developer in San Francisco.
sents.cn: 我喜欢创造事物、培育它们并解决问题，"旧金山一位成功的手机应用开发者孟丽说道，"直到身心决定'罢工'，我才真正在意自己的身心。

sents.en: "I didn't really care about my mind and my body until they decided to go on strike."
Ms. Li said her stress led to sleeplessness.
sents.cn: 孟女士说，她的压力导致了失眠。

sents.en: When she did sleep, she experienced "problem-solving dreams," which left her feeling unrested when she woke up.
sents.cn: 即便睡着了，她也会做"解决问题的梦"，醒来后反而觉得没有休息好。

sents.en: "After I became a first-time mother, I quickly realized I was so busy caring for other people and work that I felt like I'd lost myself," she said.
sents.cn: "在我初为人母之后，我很快意识到，我忙着照顾他人和工作，以至于感觉失去了自我，"她说。

sents.en: It's a common story·one we frequently ridicule and readily dismiss, for example, by claiming that women tend to complain more than men, despite the growing sum of research that underlines the problem.
sents.cn: 这是一个常见的故事——一个我们时常嘲笑、轻易忽视的故事，比如声称女性往往比男性更爱抱怨，尽管越来越多的研究都在强调这一问题。

sents.en: Women are twice as likely to suffer from severe stress and anxiety as men, according to a 2016 study published in The Journal of Brain & Behavior.
sents.cn: 根据2016年发表在《大脑与行为》期刊上的一项研究，女性遭受严重压力和焦虑的可能性是男性的两倍。

sents.en: The American Psychological Association reports a gender gap year after year showing that women consistently report higher stress levels.
sents.cn: 美国心理学会年年都报告存在性别差距，表明女性一贯报告更高的压力水平。

sents.en: Clearly, a stress gap exists.
sents.cn: 显然，压力差距确实存在。

sents.en: "The difference is not really news to me, as a clinical psychologist," said Erin Joyce, a women and couples therapist in Los Angeles.
sents.cn: "作为一名临床心理学家，这种差异对我来说并不算新闻，"洛杉矶的女性与伴侣治疗师艾琳∙乔伊斯说，"多年来大量研究充分证明，大多数焦虑障碍的患病率在女性中都高于男性。

sents.en: "It's been well documented in extensive research over the years that prevalence rates for the majority of the anxiety disorders are higher in women than men." Some people may argue that this is merely reported data, and they say many men feel the same pressures as women in terms of fulfilling responsibilities at work and home.
sents.cn: "有人可能会争辩说这仅仅是报告出来的数据，并说许多男性在履行工作和家庭责任方面感受到与女性同样的压力。

sents.en: In other words, we're all really, really stressed.
sents.cn: 换句话说，我们真的都压力山大。

sents.en: "The difference, however, is in the nature and scope of these responsibilities in the home environment in particular," Dr. Joyce said.
sents.cn: "然而，差异尤其体现在家庭环境中这些责任的性质与范围上，"乔伊斯博士说。

sents.en: For example, the United Nations reported that women do nearly three times as much unpaid domestic work as men.
sents.cn: 例如，联合国报告称，女性所做的无偿家务劳动几乎是男性的三倍。

sents.en: The problem is, housework is often overlooked as work, even though it is often as laborious (or in some cases, more so) as any paid job.
sents.cn: 问题在于，家务劳动常常被无视、不被视为工作，尽管它往往和任何有薪工作一样费力（在某些情况下甚至更甚）。

sents.en: As the scholar Silvia Federici put it in 1975, the unpaid nature of domestic work reinforces the assumption that "housework is not work, thus preventing women from struggling against it."
sents.cn: 正如学者西尔维娅∙费德里奇在1975年所言，家务劳动的无酬性质强化了一种假设，即"家务不是工作，从而阻止女性对其抗争"。

sents.en: It's not just inside the home, though.
sents.cn: 不过，这不仅仅发生在家庭内部。

sents.en: Research from Nova Southeastern University found that female managers were more likely than male managers to display "surface acting," or forcing emotions that are not wholly felt.
sents.cn: 诺瓦东南大学的研究发现，女性管理者比男性管理者更可能表现出"表面扮演"，即强迫自己表现出并未完全感受到的情绪。

sents.en: "They expressed optimism, calmness and sympathy even when these were not the emotions that they were actually feeling," the study said.
sents.cn: "即便这些并非她们真实感受到的情绪，她们也会表现出乐观、平静和同情，"该研究称。

sents.en: Surface acting is a prime example of "emotional labor," a concept that the writer Jess Zimmerman made familiar in a 2015 essay.
sents.cn: 表面扮演是"情绪劳动"的典型例子，这一概念因作家杰斯∙齐默尔曼2015年的一篇散文而广为人知。该文在互联网社区博客MetaFilter上引发了一条庞大的讨论串。

sents.en: The essay sparked a massive thread on the internet community blog MetaFilter.
sents.cn: 数百名女性谈起了自己应对情绪劳动的经历：那些被期待由她们承担、却无人察觉的职责。

sents.en: Hundreds of women spoke up about their own experience with emotional labor: the duties that are expected of them, but go unnoticed.
sents.cn: 这些无形的职责只有当你不做时才会显现。

sents.en: These invisible duties become apparent only when you don't do them.
sents.cn: 与家务劳动一样，情绪劳动通常被轻视，也不被认定为工作。

sents.en: Like domestic labor, emotional labor is generally dismissed and not labeled work.
sents.cn: 但研究表明，它可能和有薪工作一样令人筋疲力尽。

sents.en: But research shows it can be just as exhausting as paid work.
sents.cn: 情绪劳动会导致睡眠困难和家庭冲突。

sents.en: Emotional labor can lead to difficulty in sleeping and family conflict. Sure, circumstantial stress, like losing a job, may lead to these same issues.
sents.cn: 诚然，偶发性压力（如失业）也可能引发同样的问题。

sents.en: But emotional labor is not circumstantial. It's an enduring responsibility based on the socialized gender role of women.
sents.cn: 但情绪劳动并非偶发，它是基于女性社会化性别角色的持久责任。

sents.en: Like Ms. Li, many women try to manage the added stress to reach what Dr. Joyce said was an unattainable ideal.
sents.cn: 和孟女士一样，许多女性试图应对额外的压力，以达到乔伊斯博士所说的"难以企及的理想"。

sents.en: "Some professional women aim to do it all.
sents.cn: "一些职业女性立志面面俱到。

sents.en: They want to reach the top of the corporate ladder and fly like supermom," she said.
sents.cn: 她们想登上企业阶梯的顶端，像超级妈妈一样飞翔，"她说。

sents.en: When women don't reach this ideal, they feel guilty; and even more stressed.
sents.cn: 当女性未能达到这一理想时，她们会感到内疚，压力也更大。

sents.en: After her own struggle with this, Ms. Li took a step back and used her experience to build Sanity & Self, a self-care app and platform for overworked women.
sents.cn: 在自身与之抗争之后，孟女士退后一步，用自己的经历打造了Sanity&Self——一个为过度劳累的女性提供自我关怀的应用和平台。

sents.en: "The realizations I had in that process helped me gain insights and ultimately got me ready to integrate self-care into my daily life," she said.
sents.cn: "我在那一过程中获得的领悟帮我有了洞见，并最终让我准备好将自我关怀融入日常生活，"她说。

sents.en: The stress problem extends beyond mental health when you consider the link between stress, anxiety and heart health.
sents.cn: 当你考虑到压力、焦虑与心脏健康之间的联系时，压力问题就超出了心理健康范畴。

sents.en: Worse, most of what we know about heart disease comes from studies involving men.
sents.cn: 更糟的是，我们对心脏病的大部分认识都来自以男性为对象的研究。

sents.en: However, "there are many reasons to think that it's different in women," Harvard Medical School reported.
sents.cn: 然而，哈佛医学院报告称："有诸多理由认为，在女性身上情况有所不同。

sents.en: For example, women are more likely to experience disturbed sleep, anxiety and unusual fatigue before a heart attack.
sents.cn: "例如，女性在心脏病发作前更可能出现睡眠紊乱、焦虑和异常疲劳。

sents.en: Stress is so normalized that it is easy for women to shrug off those symptoms as simply the consequences of stress.
sents.cn: 压力如此常态化，以至于女性很容易把这些症状轻描淡写地归为压力的后果。

sents.en: Many women also do not experience chest pain before a heart attack the way men do, which leads to fewer women discovering problematic heart issues.
sents.cn: 许多女性在心脏病发作前也不会像男性那样经历胸痛，这导致更少女性发现心脏问题。

sents.en: Harvard reports that women are "much more likely than men to die within a year of having a heart attack" and "many women say their physicians sometimes don't even recognize the symptoms."
sents.cn: 哈佛报告称，女性"在心脏病发作后一年内死亡的可能性远高于男性"，而且"许多女性表示，她们的医生有时甚至认不出这些症状"。

sents.en: The good news is, women are more likely than men to take charge of their stress and manage it, the American Psychological Association reports.

sents.en: The concept of self-care, at its core, is quite simple.
